I noticed that between 2019 and 2020, the wage for Santa had an extreme decline by about 15% which is the only decline present. I wonder if this had to do with the Covid-19 virus that started in late 2019 in some countries, and 2020 in the United States.


2. What do you wonder?


I wonder why the wage of Santa has increased so much in the past years and has surpassed all the other jobs on this graph. Is it simply because of inflation and population growth with higher demands, or is there another factor causing this increase?


3. What impact does this have on you and your community?


This impacts the community because there are a lot of people who want to meet Santas at places like malls or superstores so the demand may be going up. Their wages are increasing more than other jobs which is surprising. This impacts the community because why are Santa's wages increasing more than essential workers like hospital workers? It seems like the wages should increase more for essential jobs like health care rather than Santas so that more people will go into healthcare and help people recover from illnesses and injuries. If hospital workers aren’t being paid enough, we might not have enough doctors and that could be a danger to the community.


4. Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.

“Santa’s Big Raise”

## 1. Chart type
- **Multi-series line chart**

## 2. Layout techniques
- Uses **multiple lines in a single panel**
- No faceting or small multiples
- No stacking
- Series are distinguished primarily by **color** and **direct end labels**

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Year (2015–2022) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Average wage growth since 2015 (%) | Quantitative | Position on y-axis |
| Worker group / occupation category (Santa, Leisure & hospitality, Retail, All workers, Hospitals, Managers) | Categorical/nominal | Line color/lightness, separate line series, direct text labels at line ends |
raw_comment:
1. What do you notice?
Santa has been increasing their worker’s wages the most since 2020 and 2022 from nearly +5% to +43% (compared to 2015). Santa’s average wage growth dipped in 2019 to 2020 from +20% to just +5% (compared to 2015). All other sections of work such as leisure and hospitality, all workers, hospitals, managers and retail all increased near linearly from 2015 to 2020 (+0% to +13%-20%) then jumped in 2020 to 2023 increasing again linearly but about +5% to +10% per year depending on section (since 2015). 


2. What do you wonder?
I wonder why wage increases didn’t dip in all the other districts in 2020 (other than Santa). Were they not as damaged by the pandemic than Santa? I also wonder what occurred in 2016 to 2017 caused Santa to slow the wage growth (since 2015). I wonder why hospitals and managers are not seeing the same job growth as the other departments. 

3. What impact does this have on you and your community?
This aids our communities especially in leisure and hospitality and retail with wage growth. Santa is also paying their workers even more with a +43% average wage growth since 2015. Managers on the other hand (along with hospitals and all workers) are not seeing as much wage growth since 2015 as the other sections of work.

4. Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
Consider This Year Working for Santa! +43% Job Growth Since 2015!!!
